name: NYC 2015 Street Tree Census
coverage: All 5 NYC boroughs (Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island)
used_for: Tree identity, location (GPS), diameter at breast height (DBH), health status, species
notes: The 2015 census was conducted by 2,000+ volunteers coordinated by NYC Parks & Recreation. It is the authoritative source for NYC street tree positions and species. ROOT uses this dataset to identify every tree threatened by a removal permit.

name: USDA i-Tree Eco — NYC Ecosystem Valuation
used_for: Annual ecosystem service valuations: stormwater interception (gal/yr), CO₂ storage (lbs/yr), cooling energy (kWh/yr), air quality improvement (USD/yr)
methodology: Per-inch-DBH annual benefit coefficients for NYC's Humid Subtropical climate zone, updated with 2024 NYC utility pricing. Stormwater: $0.14/gal (NYC DEP green infrastructure avoided-cost value). CO₂: $0.045/lb ($100/ton, EPA 2023 interim social cost of carbon). Electricity: $0.22/kWh (NYC ConEd avg residential, 2024). Air quality: $3.20/inch-DBH-year (PM2.5 + O₃ + NO₂, NYC 2023).
notes: Coefficients derived from published USDA i-Tree research for the NYC metro region. All figures are annual averages — actual values vary by species, site, and growing conditions.

name: EPA EJScreen — Environmental Justice Screening Tool
used_for: Heat vulnerability percentile scores by census tract. ROOT uses these scores to flag tree removal permits in Environmental Justice communities where urban heat island impacts are highest.
notes: EJScreen indexes include PM2.5, ozone, toxic releases, and heat vulnerability. ROOT surfaces the heat vulnerability index (HVEI) which is especially relevant for tree canopy loss.

name: NYC Department of Buildings — Job Filings
used_for: New building and alteration permits. ROOT cross-references DOB job filings with NYC Parks tree work permits to identify cases where construction projects threaten street trees.
notes: Job types A2 (major alteration) and NB (new building) are the most common triggers for tree removal. ROOT focuses on permits within the tree pit buffer zone.

name: NYC Parks — Tree Work Orders
used_for: Tree removal work orders and planting inspection records. ROOT queries this dataset during the 12-month and 36-month follow-up checks to verify whether replacement trees were actually planted and survived.
notes: The ForMS (Forestry Management System) is the authoritative Parks database for tree work. ROOT uses the public extract to check replacement planting status.

name: NYC Administrative Code § 18-107
used_for: Legal citation in public comments. § 18-107 governs street tree protections and replacement requirements for construction projects in NYC.
notes: Requires developers to obtain a permit and provide replacement trees for any street tree removed. ROOT cites this code in generated public comments to ground the intervention in existing law.

name: OneNYC 2050 — 30% Urban Tree Canopy Target
publisher: NYC Mayor's Office of Long-Term Planning and Sustainability
used_for: Policy benchmark cited in ROOT's impact calculations and public comments. NYC committed to increasing urban tree canopy cover to 30% by 2035 under the OneNYC 2050 plan.
notes: As of 2020, NYC canopy cover was approximately 22%. The 30% target requires net tree gain, making developer replacement compliance a key policy instrument.
